codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly extends SpaController to handle all 5 response types from the protocol dispatcher (FaultLogResponse, FilterCyclesResponse, InformationResponse, ConfigurationResponse, ControlConfiguration). New ControllerEvent variants are added, storage fields and accessor methods are properly implemented, and process_bytes() correctly dispatches each IncomingMessage variant to its typed event. 14 new tests provide comprehensive coverage of all response types, data fidelity, mixed events, registration non-interference, pump timer non-interference, and accessor behavior. The code follows existing patterns in the crate and maintains clean separation of concerns.

issues.description: Test test_controller_handles_configuration_response (VAL-MQTT-028) uses Command::ConfigurationRequest which triggers SpaSim's 0x04 handler, generating a 0x2E (ControlConfiguration) response — NOT a 0x94 (ConfigurationResponse). The test asserts ControlConfiguration event and stores in last_control_config(). This means the ConfigurationResponse variant (0x94) and last_config() accessor are never exercised in any test. The protocol dispatcher has a distinct 0x94 sub-type for ConfigurationResponse, but SpaSim's generate_config_response() always produces 0x2E. While the implementation code is correct (the match arm for IncomingMessage::ConfigurationResponse does work), this is a test coverage gap — no test validates the ConfigurationResponse path end-to-end.

sharedStateObservations.observation: SpaSim's generate_config_response() always produces a 0x2E (ControlConfiguration) response, never a 0x94 (ConfigurationResponse). The dispatcher has distinct IncomingMessage variants for both (ControlConfiguration vs ConfigurationResponse), but the sim only supports generating ControlConfiguration. This means the ConfigurationResponse path through SpaController cannot be integration-tested with the current sim. This is documented nowhere but affects anyone writing integration tests involving configuration responses.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: crates/launa-sim/src/spa_sim.rs:935 — full_payload starts with 0x2E. The dispatcher at crates/launa-protocol/src/dispatcher.rs maps 0x2E to ControlConfiguration and 0x94 to ConfigurationResponse separately.

sharedStateObservations.observation: SpaController in launa-sim has a force_registered() helper method (line ~340) for tests to bypass the normal registration flow, and tests can use make_registered_sim() helper to get a SpaSim with completed registration via the protocol flow (sending ID request bytes). This pattern of having dual helpers (one bypassing, one protocol-faithful) is useful for different test scenarios.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: crates/launa-sim/src/controller.rs force_registered() method and make_registered_sim() test helper

summary: The implementation is well-structured and correctly handles all 5 response types from the protocol dispatcher. The code cleanly extends the existing SpaController without disrupting registration flow or pump timers. 14 new tests cover all assertions (VAL-MQTT-025 through VAL-MQTT-033) with thorough data fidelity verification. One non-blocking observation: ConfigurationResponse (0x94) is never generated by SpaSim, so the last_config() accessor and ConfigurationResponse event variant have no end-to-end test coverage — only ControlConfiguration (0x2E) is exercised. The implementation code itself is correct; this is a sim tooling gap rather than a bug.
